title: Exposing Kubernetes to the internet? Do this first
caption: How do you route external traffic to your Kubernetes cluster?

scenes.vo: How do users on the internet actually reach your Kubernetes Pods? You expose them using a LoadBalancer Service!
scenes.heading: LOADBALANCER

scenes.vo: Think of it like a receptionist at a busy office directing visitors to open desks.
scenes.heading: THE ANALOGY
scenes.line: A receptionist guiding visitors to open desks

scenes.vo: Traffic hits a public cloud IP address, routes to the Service, and gets distributed across healthy Pods.
scenes.heading: TRAFFIC FLOW

scenes.vo: If one Pod fails, the LoadBalancer instantly detects it and routes traffic only to healthy Pods.
scenes.heading: POD FAILURE

scenes.vo: Skip manual cloud setup. Just set type to LoadBalancer inside your Service spec!
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.vo: So, LoadBalancer Services: provide public IPs, balance traffic, and handle failures automatically. Follow for more Kubernetes tips!
scenes.heading: LOADBALANCER
